html:
Most TikTok Shop GMV problems trace back to the same handful of mistakes: recruiting creators by follower count, running a weak offer, over-scripting content, ignoring your winners, and measuring effort instead of sales. None of them are dramatic, which is why they persist. Here are the five, and the fix for each.

Mistake 1: Recruiting by follower count

The problem: you chase big accounts and ignore mid-size creators who actually sell your category. A 400,000-follower lifestyle account that has never moved a product loses to a 40,000-follower creator who sells your niche weekly.

The fix: recruit by selling behavior, not reach. Filter for category selling history first, follower count last.

There is a sixth mistake worth naming up front, because it undoes the other five: picking products by margin instead of by what sells. Marketer Neil Patel put it sharply: brands "get serious about TikTok Shop, open their catalog, and pick the products with the best margins. That's exactly why they lose," noting that "81% of everything on TikTok Shop sells for under $30" (@neilpatel on X). Treat that 81% figure as his claim rather than gospel, but the lesson holds: fight the platform's price reality and no creator program saves you.

Mistake 2: A weak offer

The problem: low commission, no creative freedom, a product with thin reviews. Good creators skip you because there is nothing in it for them.

The fix: set commission by margin, go higher to recruit when you are new, offer real creative freedom, and fix your listing's conversion before blaming creators.

Mistake 3: Over-scripting content

The problem: you hand creators a word-for-word script and a shot list, and the result feels like an ad, which is exactly what viewers scroll past and the algorithm buries.

The fix: brief the few things that must be right, hook, proof, compliance, and hand creators freedom on the rest. Use a light brief template and the hook formulas.

Mistake 4: Ignoring your winners

The problem: you spread attention evenly across every creator, when affiliate GMV is concentrated in a few. The winners get the same treatment as the non-responders.

The fix: spot the creators who sell and double down immediately, more product, better commission, bigger collaborations, and amplify their content with ads.

Mistake 5: Measuring the wrong thing

The problem: you track messages sent, creators contacted, or raw follower reach, none of which is sales. You feel busy and GMV does not move.

The fix: measure GMV, GMV per creator, post rate, and organic vs ad split. Effort metrics feel good and tell you nothing.

The pattern behind all five

Every one of these is a shortcut: the follower number instead of selling history, the script instead of trust, the even spread instead of the hard call on winners. TikTok Shop rewards the unglamorous system, not the shortcut.

The takeaway

Fix these five and GMV usually moves without any new tactic: recruit by selling, strengthen the offer, brief lightly, back your winners, and measure sales. If you would rather have someone run the system for you, that is what an agency is for.

Want a second set of eyes on your program? Book a call, or find better-fit creators to start.
